subject: Post-call: deployment path checklist & allowlist/network asks
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliobank.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Sep 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment path checklist & allowlist/network asks

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (short):
- HelioBank is evaluating Private VPC first (primary), but still wants a clear fallback plan to Dedicated if timelines/ops block PrivateLink peering.
- Key constraints: regulated data residency (US-only), strict egress IP allowlist, and internal policy that limits wide VPC peering across accounts.

What we need from you to scope PrivateLink (preferred):
1) Confirmation that HelioBank allows AWS Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) to be created pointing at our endpoint service (yes/no).
2) Target VPC ID(s) and VPC CIDR(s) for endpoint placement (format: vpc-12345 / 10.0.0.0/16).
3) Account ID(s) that will accept the PrivateLink connections (12-digit AWS Account ID).
4) Any required static egress IPs that must be whitelisted on your side for callbacks/metrics (we can provide our NAT/eproxy IP list).
5) KMS preference: do you require customer-managed keys (BYOK) in your account, or are you comfortable with a Redwood-managed key in a dedicated deployment?

Notes on options (short):
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): avoids peering, supports private traffic into your VPC; requires endpoint creation and VPC endpoint permissions. Good for tightly controlled networks.
- VPC Peering: possible but often blocked for regulated customers that forbid cross-account peering. Simpler networking but less isolation control.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed capacity): fastest to spin up but does not place inference nodes inside your VPC; we can provide static egress IPs and contractual SLAs.

Attachments: I attached a short "network-ask" template to collect VPC IDs, CIDRs, and contact points — please fill and return when convenient. Also attached a short note on our KMS support.

Immediate next steps we propose:
- HelioBank: confirm items 1–5 above and share the filled template (target by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: once we get the template, we’ll produce a deployment checklist and an environment-specific list of egress IPs and ports (expected 24–48 hrs).
- Optional: schedule a 30-min technical sync between HelioBank NetOps and our infra lead (Aditya) — suggest Mon 09/08.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to the filled template so we can scope deployment timelines.

Best,
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
mobile: (415) 555-0123

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliobank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioBank Network Team <netops@heliobank.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path checklist & allowlist/network asks

Thanks Michael — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PrivateLink is preferred by our security/compliance team because peering across vendor accounts is restricted by policy. So yes, we lean to PrivateLink but we need to validate feasibility with NetOps.
2) We cannot host keys in Redwood-managed KMS for production data. BYOK in our account is a hard requirement for PII workloads. Please confirm Redwood supports BYOK for Private deployments and what minimal permissions you require.
3) Egress IPs: we will only accept a short list of static IPs for outbound callbacks and telemetry. Can you provide those? If you cannot guarantee a stable set, we will need to consider Dedicated within our VPC/colocation options.
4) We will fill the attached template and return it — ETA EOD Wed as requested.

NetOps note (from NetOps alias): we will need a short doc listing ports/health-check IPs, expected TLS behavior (mTLS or mutual certs?), and whether the endpoint service requires accepting (allow) your account ID before we create the interface endpoints.

We will set up a 30-min sync for Mon 09/08 10:00am PT with Aditya if that works for your team.

—Priya
Head of Cloud Infrastructure
HelioBank

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliobank.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Sep 2027 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path checklist & allowlist/network asks

Priya — great, thanks for confirming the preference and BYOK requirement. Short answers and what we’ll produce before the Mon sync: 

- BYOK support: yes — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys in Private deployments. For AWS that typically looks like either:
  * Customer creates a CMK in their account and grants Redwood's service principal access (we document the grant policy), OR
  * Customer uses an AWS KMS grant scoped to the key for our service role.
We will attach a one-page "KMS integration checklist" and a minimal IAM permissions snippet you can share with security. (see attached redwood-kms-notes.pdf)

- Egress IPs: we can provide a short, stable set of NAT egress IPs for control-plane callbacks and metrics endpoints; those IPs are static for each deployment and we will publish them in the deployment checklist. Draft egress list will be sent 24–48 hours after we get the VPC template.

- mTLS vs TLS: our control plane currently uses TLS with client cert validation as an option for Private deployments; NetOps can opt-in to mTLS for additional assurance. We’ll add that as an explicit configuration item.

What we need from NetOps for the sync (short):
- VPC ID(s) + CIDR blocks you intend to use for interface endpoints.
- AWS Account ID(s) that will accept the endpoint connection.
- If you have a security contact who will own the KMS grant flow (name + email).

I’ve attached the KMS notes and re-attached the network template. Aditya — can you prepare the draft egress IP list once we have the filled template?

Thanks — see you Monday.

Best,
Michael

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@heliobank.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Sep 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment path checklist & allowlist/network asks

On Wed, Sep 7, 2027 at 08:02 AM Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ve attached the KMS notes and re-attached the network template. Aditya — can you prepare the draft egress IP list once we have the filled template?

Will do. Quick internal note for HelioBank: our typical PrivateLink architecture uses an internal NLB in the Redwood account fronting inference nodes, and customers create interface endpoints in their VPC pointed at our endpoint service. We will provide: 

- NLB DNS names and the list of associated static egress IPs (for control-plane callbacks),
- Health-check IPs and required ports (443 + health-check port as needed),
- A short example of the AWS endpoint-service policy that HelioBank must accept to allow endpoint creation.

I’ve attached a preliminary egress-ips CSV (egress-ips-v2.csv) with placeholder ranges — we’ll finalize once we receive your VPC CIDRs and account IDs.

See you on Mon 09/08 for the netops sync — Aditya (infra lead) will present the deployment flow and the KMS grant steps.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Infra Lead 
Redwood Inference
